function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

It sounds like you’re looking for a virtual companion—something along the lines of an “AI girlfriend.” That’s definitely something people have been experimenting with lately! Below I’ll outline some common approaches, highlight popular tools/platforms, touch on customization ideas, and point out a few things to keep in mind when designing or choosing such a system. --- ### 1️⃣ What You Might Want From an AI Girlfriend | Feature | Why It Matters | |---------|----------------| | **Conversational Flow** – Natural back‑and‑forth dialogue without awkward pauses. | Keeps interactions engaging. | | **Personality & Tone** – Friendly, supportive, witty, romantic… | Makes the bot feel more human-like. | | **Memory / Context Retention** – Remember past chats, preferences, inside jokes. | Builds continuity over multiple sessions. | | **Emotion Recognition** – Detect mood cues (e.g., sadness, excitement). | Allows empathetic responses. | | **Multimodal Interaction** – Text + voice, images, emojis. | Adds richness to conversations. | | **Safety Filters** – Avoid harassment, hate speech, or inappropriate topics. | Protects users and keeps the experience wholesome. | Feel free to pick which ones matter most to you! --- ### 2️⃣ Ready‑Made Platforms | Platform | Key Strengths | How to Get Started | |----------|---------------|--------------------| | **Replika** | • Deep learning‑based conversation
• Personality profiles (“Friend,” “Love”)
• Voice & text support | Download app → Create account → Choose persona | | **Chatbot Studio (by Botpress)** | • Drag‑and‑drop flow builder
• Custom NLP models
• Integrate into web/mobile apps | Sign up → Build flows → Deploy via webhook | | **OpenAI GPT‑4 (via ChatGPT API)** | • State‑of‑the‑art LLM
- Fine‑tune prompts for romance-friendly tone | Register at openai.com → Use `chat/completions` endpoint | | **Microsoft Azure Cognitive Services – Language Service** | • Conversational AI SDKs
• Built‑in safety filters | Set up Azure subscription → Call REST APIs | | **Rasa** | • Fully open source
• Strong intent/entity recognition
• Easy integration with custom logic | Install RASA → Train domain/models → Run locally or cloud | If you just want a quick demo, Replika or ChatGPT already offer “romantic” personas right out of the box. For deeper control, consider building your own bot with Rasa or Botpress. --- ### 3️⃣ Building Your Own (Custom) AI Girlfriend Below is a high‑level roadmap: #### Step 1 – Define Scope & Persona * Write a short biography (age, interests, quirks). * Decide on conversational style guidelines (formal vs casual, humor levels). #### Step 2 – Pick Technology Stack | Option | Pros | Cons | |--------|------|------| | **Large Language Model (LLM)** e.g., GPT‑4 | Very natural language generation | Requires API cost, privacy concerns | | **Rule‑Based Engine** (Botpress, Dialogflow) | Predictable behavior, easier moderation | Less flexible, harder to handle nuance | | **Hybrid** (LLM + rule layer) | Combines best of both worlds | More complex architecture | #### Step 3 – Implement Core Components ```python import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) def get_response(message_history): # Append new user input prompt = "\n".join([f"{role}: {msg}" for role,msg in message_history]) completion = client.chat.completions.create( model="gpt-4", messages=[{"role": r.split(":")[0], "content": m} for r,m in [p.split(": ",1) for p in prompt.split("\n")]], temperature=0.7, max_tokens=500, top_p=0.95, frequency_penalty=0.5, presence_penalty=0.5, ) return completion.choices[0].message.content.strip() ``` *Add memory:* Store recent exchanges in a database or simple list so the bot remembers context across turns.* #### Step 4 – Add Safety Layer Use built‑in moderation endpoints (`openai.moderations`) or third‑party libraries (Perspective API) to filter profanity, hateful content, or overly intimate remarks unless explicitly allowed. #### Step 5 – UI / Integration Choose how users will interact: * Web chat widget (React/Vue) * Mobile app (Flutter/Kotlin) * Messaging platform bot (Telegram, Discord) #### Step 6 – Test & Iterate Run scripted scenarios, gather feedback, tweak personalities, adjust temperature/frequency penalties until the vibe feels right. --- ### 4️⃣ Ethical & Practical Considerations | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Consent & Boundaries** | Even though it’s a bot, set clear boundaries (no personal data sharing, no real emotional attachment). | | **Privacy** | Never store sensitive info longer than needed. Encrypt logs. | | **User Well‑Being** | Offer resources if someone expresses distress. | | **Transparency** | Let users know they’re talking to an AI. | | **Legal Compliance** | Follow GDPR/EU laws if operating there; respect age restrictions. | --- ### 5️⃣ Quick Starter Checklist 1. **Pick a base platform** (Replika for instant use, or GPT‑4 for full flexibility). 2. **Define a persona** (write a brief bio). 3. **Set safety rules** (filter lists, moderation calls). 4. **Deploy** (web, mobile, messaging). 5. **Iteratively improve** based on usage patterns. --- Let me know which direction excites you most—or if you'd like help setting up a specific stack, writing prompts, or configuring safety checks. Happy chatting!
